open_points.subject: M08 AdmissionVerdict identity and repeated admission
open_points.text: “Substitution: a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict.” But “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time, and the verdict covers exactly those executions,” while TrialExecutions are separately minted observations.
open_points.question: When the same implementation is admitted again against an unchanged corpus, is the existing AdmissionVerdict reused, or is a new verdict created from new TrialExecutions; if new, what distinguishes its identity?
options: Reuse the existing verdict and its original TrialExecutions
Create a new entity verdict for every admission run
Create a new value verdict whose identity includes the newly minted TrialExecutions
open_points.default_guess: Reuse the existing verdict for the same implementation and corpus.

open_points.subject: M17 ProofResult
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result.” But a proof may fail because a binding is not accepted and the same flow version may be proven again after that binding is accepted.
open_points.question: What current external facts are part of a ProofResult's meaning or identity, so that two proofs of the same unchanged flow version may legitimately differ?
options: Include the relevant binding statuses or a digest of proof dependencies
Treat each proof as a separately identified observation
Define ProofResult as an ephemeral answer with no stable identity
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an ephemeral value determined by the flow version plus the current binding states.

open_points.subject: M23 NodeExecution
open_points.text: Its Identity is declared “value,” but its evidence says “an attempt's record is issued once,” while comparable issued observations and selections in M07, M09, M18 and M26 are entities.
open_points.question: Is a NodeExecution a value identified by all of its facts, or an entity representing one issued attempt and identified by run_id, node_id, map_index and attempt_number?
options: Value identified by all meaning facts
Entity identified by its attempt coordinates
Entity with a separately minted identifier
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an entity identified by run_id, node_id, map_index and attempt_number.

open_points.subject: Inspection action and model readership
open_points.text: State 0 permits owner and agent to “inspect functions, flows, runs, bindings, approvals, standing grants and effect attempts,” but State 1 does not say which constituent records or facts make up the typed descriptions of functions and flows, and M11, M25 and M26 do not name inspection as a reader.
open_points.question: Exactly which State 1 models and facts are returned by each inspectable product object, including whether function inspection exposes contracts, implementation code, activations, trial cases, trial executions and verdicts, and whether flow inspection exposes versions, proofs and activations?
options: Inspection returns every constituent record and fact, subject to personal-data masking
Inspection returns only a summary projection, with repair-specific evidence supplied separately
Each named object has an explicitly enumerated inspection projection
open_points.default_guess: Define an explicit projection for each inspectable object, exposing implementation code and trial evidence only through the one-slot repair view required by K-12.

open_points.subject: Capture of a failed execution after its run ends
open_points.text: The capture action refuses an execution “whose run was already released (its files are gone),” and M06 repeats only that exclusion, but K-10 says every non-failed run's spool is emptied when the run ends; therefore files are also gone after a run ends refused or cancelled.
open_points.question: Can a failed function execution be captured after its run ends refused or cancelled, and does eligibility differ between cases containing only stored values and cases requiring spooled file inputs?
options: Only executions from failed, unreleased runs may be captured after run end
Any failed execution may be captured while its required bytes still exist; value-only executions remain capturable later
All executions from refused or cancelled runs are permanently ineligible
open_points.default_guess: Permit capture exactly while all required inputs still exist: value-only failures remain capturable, while failures needing spool files are refused after any event that empties the spool.
